content.title: Initialize library-release expertise
content.description:
Initialize your expertise index with full project context.

Read these files to build your knowledge:
- packages/library/package.json (dependencies, scripts, exports)
- packages/library/tsup.config.ts (build config)
- packages/library/typedoc.json (docs config)
- packages/library/tsconfig.json (TypeScript config)
- packages/library/eslint.config.js (linting)
- packages/library/.prettierrc (formatting)
- packages/library/src/index.ts (programmatic API entry)
- packages/library/src/bin.ts (CLI entry)

Run these commands to understand the current state:
- cd packages/library && bun run quality (all quality gates)
- cd packages/library && bun run build (produce dist artifacts)
- cd packages/library && bun run docs (generate TypeDoc HTML)

Document in your expertise index:
1. Project overview: trackgentic is an npm library (TypeScript, Bun) for AI agent issue tracking
2. Build pipeline: tsup produces ESM plus CJS plus dts plus CLI binary to dist folder
3. Documentation: TypeDoc HTML output to docs-html folder
4. Tests: Bun test runner, 569+ tests, quality gate via bun run quality
5. Quality gates: strict TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier, coverage thresholds
6. Release workflow: CI on every push, release on version tag, npm publish plus GitHub Pages docs
7. Your responsibilities: release prep, documentation, build, version management, publishing
8. Your team: manager is cto, peers are library-developer and library-quality
9. Note: library-quality no longer owns documentation tasks, you do

Write your expertise to your index file, then comment here with your findings.

content.content: This is your first task as a new team member. Take your time to thoroughly read the project files and build a comprehensive understanding. Your expertise index is your long-term memory - make it detailed enough that you can work autonomously on future release tasks. Focus especially on the build pipeline, quality gates, and release workflow since those are your primary responsibilities.

Expertise initialization complete. Here are my findings:

**Project Overview**: agentrack is an npm library (TypeScript, Bun) for AI agent issue tracking — file-backed, event-sourced, git-friendly. Version 0.1.0.

**Build Pipeline**: tsup v8.5.1 with two targets:
- Library (src/index.ts): ESM + CJS + DTS → dist/index.js, dist/index.cjs, dist/index.d.ts, dist/index.d.cts + sourcemaps. Commander kept external for tree-shaking.
- CLI (src/bin.ts): Bundled ESM standalone → dist/bin.js with node shebang. Registered as 'agt' binary.

**Documentation**: TypeDoc v0.28.19, output to docs-html/, entry at src/index.ts, categories [Core, Types, Errors]. Command: bun run docs. Check: bun run docs:check.

**Tests**: 573 tests across 25 files, all passing. Core modules 93-100% coverage. CLI commands have low coverage (unit tests focus on core). Runner: bun test v1.3.11.

**Quality Gates**: bun run quality = typecheck + lint + test:coverage. All pass cleanly. prepublishOnly also runs quality.

**TypeScript**: Strict mode with extra checks (noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, noImplicitOverride, noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature).

**Release Workflow**: CI on every push, release on version tag, npm publish + GitHub Pages docs.

**Note**: I was unable to write my expertise index file due to file permissions on .agentic/expertise/. The file needs to be written to /Users/javi/projects/agentrack/.agentic/expertise/library-release/library-release-index.yaml — please grant write access or let me know an alternative path.
